question: Does perfect foreknowledge make an actual petition normatively idle?
bounded_conclusion: Omniscience alone does not rule out a noninformational authorizing role for a request, given a temporal agent and a defensible act-constituted permission norm.
not_established: that every conception of God is temporal or responsive
that a request creates an obligation to grant it
that prayer changes outcomes or welfare
that the view is original or accurately represents the literature

terms.foreknowledge: Knowing before t1 that a request will occur at t1.
terms.request_event: The actual performance of the petition at t1.
terms.authorization: A normative permission that may be constituted by an actual invitation under an applicable norm.
terms.answering_relation: The response at t2 stands in a relation to the performed request, not merely to prior knowledge of its content.

premises.claim: Some legitimate permissions are constituted by the actual invitation or consent, not by an observer's evidence that such an act will occur.
Knowledge of a future speech act is not identical to performance of that act; the normative fact may be indexed to occurrence.
premises.status: conceptual distinction; requires source and counterargument testing

premises.claim: A temporal agent can adopt a conditional policy that waits for an invitation despite knowing it will occur.
premises.status: model assumption; compatible with foreknowledge in the stipulated case, but does not solve all foreknowledge/free-will debates

premises.claim: After the invitation, the same action can be permitted and count as an answer without the request adding information.
premises.status: follows only if P1 and the policy apply

premises.claim: Omniscience alone does not entail that future permissions already obtain or that event-performance is reducible to knowledge.
premises.status: limited modal premise; requires closest-source tests

inference.type: conditional application to the temporal model
defeats entailment from omniscience to normative idleness

strongest_objection.claim: Perfect goodness and foreknowledge already include all relevant facts; a divine agent has no need for human consent norms, while timelessness excludes a before/after authorization change.
strongest_objection.reply: O1 needs premises beyond omniscience. The argument preserves only the temporal-model possibility and concedes that O1 may defeat application to particular divine conceptions.
strongest_objection.residual_risk: No timeless response relation or divine consent norm has been defended here.

times: t0: listener knows the future request
t2: listener gives a stipulated welfare-neutral acknowledgment
controlled_features: same words and material result stipulated
worked_case.purpose: Test the inference from foreknowledge to normative redundancy; not evidence about actual divine action.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Can authorization matter when it is timelessly or infallibly known?
assessor_engagement.response: Answer only the temporal infallible-foreknowledge case; timelessness remains unresolved.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Perfect goodness and foreknowledge may eliminate the timing distinction, and finite-human consent may not transfer.
assessor_engagement.response: Treat as a possible defeat of divine application; do not infer that the analogy establishes the theological claim.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Specify temporality and divine agency; test prayer precedents.
assessor_engagement.response: Bound thesis to temporal agency and reserve source work for the next probe.
